identity.author: John Davenant

identity.edition: Dissertationes duae (Cambridge: Roger Daniel, 1650). Partial through Cap. X Propos. 3 open. Further Cap. X remains.

scope.locus: De praedestinatione Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2 cont. + Propos. 3 open.
scope.next_locus: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 3 cont. (Aug. contra 2 Epist. Pelag. / De praedest. sanct. 14 / De bono pers. 15; Prosper; then close of Cap. X / Cap. XI if any).

sections.title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2: why not to all need not trouble the believer who holds just condemnation in Adam; Epist. 107 — Grace of God is not given to all men
english: Why it is not given to all need not trouble the believer who holds that from one all went into most just condemnation. Not to pile witnesses: I add only Epistle 107, where among twelve sentences he affirms belong to catholic faith, the second is: The grace of God is not given to all men.
sections.latin: Cur autem non omnibus detur, fidelem movere non debet, qui credit ex uno omnes isse in condemnationem justissimam. Ne nimis multus sim in accumulandis testimoniis, illud unicum adjungam quod exstat Epistola cvii. in qua, inter duodecim illas sententias quae ad fidem Catholicam pertinere affirmat, haec secunda est, Gratiam Dei non dari omnibus hominibus.

sections.title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2: Epist. 107 means regenerating, sanctifying, saving grace—not Arminius’s common illuminating grace; nor ‘given because they willed’
english: Those words—even Arminius judging—do not point to illuminating, exciting, persuading grace (which he makes common to all mortals), but to regenerating, sanctifying, saving grace. Nor can they hide here: that vivifying, saving grace is in fact given to some because they willed to take it, and withheld from others because they willed to refuse. In that same epistle it is Pelagian to hold this grace is given because we will; Orthodox that by this grace God makes us will. Add: this grace’s condition and power is that no hard heart refuses it, because it is given first to take hardness of heart away.
sections.latin: Quae verba, ne Arminio quidem arbitro, ad illam illuminantem, excitantem, et suadentem gratiam sunt referenda; (nam illam facit omnibus mortalibus communem) sed ad regenerantem, sanctificantem, et salvantem. Neque hic abdere se possunt in illud latibulum, Hanc gratiam vivificantem et salvantem dari de facto quibusdam, quia voluerunt illam accipere; non dari aliis, quia voluerunt respuere. Nam in illa ipsa Epistola Pelagianum habetur, statuere, hanc gratiam dari nobis quia volumus; Orthodoxum per hanc gratiam Deum efficere ut velimus. Huc adde, Hanc esse hujus gratiae conditionem ac virtutem, ut nullo duro corde respuatur, quia in hoc datur ut cordis durities primitus auferatur.

sections.title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2: Prosper — God foresaw whom he would give to believe; liberating grace prepared for some, not others; saving grace passes some by
english: Prosper agrees with Augustine (Ad Excerpta Genovensium, dub. 8): Let us wisely and piously confess that God immutably foresaw to whom he would give belief, or whom he would give to his Son so as to lose none of them—and that this is the saints’ predestination: foresight and preparation of the grace by which they are most certainly freed. The rest, not freed, whom grace did not exempt from humankind’s general perdition, we must know by just judgment not exempted. He sets liberating grace prepared and given to some; he denies it prepared or given to others. In De ingratis 12 the Pelagian dogma is that Christ’s grace passes by no one born; and De vocatione Gentium 2.13 he expressly asserts that the Savior’s grace passes some by.
sections.latin: Ab Augustino non dissentit Prosper: Ad Excerpt. Gen. dub. 8. Agnoscamus, inquit, sapienter pieque fateamur; praescisse incommutabiliter Deum quibus esset daturus ut crederent, aut quos daturus esset Filio suo, ut ex eis non perderet quemquam. Et hanc esse praedestinationem sanctorum, praescientiam scilicet et praeparationem gratiae Dei qua certissime liberantur. Caeteros autem, quicunque non liberantur, quos a generali perditione humani generis gratia non exemit, justo noverimus judicio non exemptos. Ponit gratiam liberantem praeparatam et donatam aliquibus; negat eandem praeparatam aut donatam aliis. Et in libro De ingratis, cap. 12. Pelagianum dogma habetur, Quod gratia Christi Nullum omnino hominem de cunctis qui generantur Praetereat. Et de vocatione Gentium, lib. 2. cap. 13. diserte asserit, Salvantis gratiam aliquos praeterire.

sections.title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2 close: Milevis and Orange preach justifying/converting inspiration not given promiscuously to all — Synod of African exiles in Sardinia
english: Turn to the councils: in them such a Grace of Christ is preached as experience itself cries is not given promiscuously to all. Milevis declares (can. 3–5) that the grace of God given through Jesus Christ is the grace of justification—and no one doubts that this (whatever is said of exciting and illuminating grace) is not common to all. Orange teaches the same (can. 5): the grace now in question is the Holy Spirit’s inspiration correcting our will from unbelief to faith, from impiety to piety. That such efficacious inspiration is given to some and not others is so plain that to deny it is folly, not mere ignorance. Best and most express is the Synodical Letter of the bishops exiled in Sardinia: He does not think worthily of grace who thinks it is given to all men. A little later they name the grace they mean—the one that works in a man both to will and to do—and add: This it works in his own, that they may work their salvation. Who are those God owns? Presently: All the predestined themselves are those God wills to be saved. So some never had this grace efficacious to salvation given or destined to them.
sections.latin: Verum ad Concilia transeamus, de quibus illud generatim affirmare licet, Gratiam Christi talem in illis praedicari, qualem omnibus non dari promiscue clamat ipsa experientia. Milevitanum, Gratiam Dei per Jesum Christum nobis donatam, gratiam justificationis esse, declarat, can. 3, 4, et 5. Hanc autem (quicquid de excitante et illuminante gratia statuatur) non esse omnium communem nemo dubitat. Eadem est sententia Arausicani, quod docet hanc gratiam de qua nunc quaeritur, esse inspirationem Spiritus sancti corrigentem voluntatem nostram ab infidelitate ad fidem, ab impietate ad pietatem, Can. 5. Talem autem ac tam efficacem inspirationem aliquibus dari, aliquibus non dari, adeo manifestum est, ut non inscitiae solum, sed stultitiae sit illud negare. Denique, habemus optimum et maxime expressum testimonium in Epistola Synodica Episcoporum in Sardinia exsulantium. Sic igitur illi; De gratia non digne sentit, quisquis eam putat omnibus hominibus dari. Paulo post ostendunt quam gratiam intelligunt, nempe eam quae in homine operatur et velle et facere. Pergunt, atque explicant insuper in quibus Dei gratia hoc operatur; Hoc, inquiunt, operatur in suis, ut suam salutem operentur. Sed quinam tandem sunt illi quos Deus pro suis agnoscit? Mox sequitur; Omnes praedestinati ipsi sunt quos Deus vult salvos fieri. Ex quibus omnibus consequitur, Esse aliquos quibus nec data nec destinata unquam fuit haec gratia efficax ad salutem.

sections.title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2→3 bridge: Orthodox consent — regenerating Grace of Christ not to all but to God’s peculiar own; Propos. 3 opens on mere mercy without prior person-difference
english: From Orthodox consent you see: the Grace of Christ properly so called—regenerating and saving—is not given to all, but to certain persons God peculiarly claims as his. The last proposition remains, which most holds the cause, and which all the Orthodox confessed no less than the two before. That Grace of Christ which consists in infusing faith, charity, and every gift needed to effect salvation infallibly—that is, which heals the soul and gives to will and finish the good—is not given from prior regard to some better acts or dispositions in the receivers, nor denied from prior regard to worse acts or dispositions in non-receivers, but from God’s mere will of mercy on whom he wills and non-mercy on whom he wills not, with no respect to a prior difference of persons.
sections.latin: Videtis jam ex consensu Orthodoxorum, Gratiam Christi proprie dictam, hoc est, regenerantem et salvantem, non dari omnibus, sed certis personis quas pro suis Deus peculiariter vendicat. Restat ultima propositio, quae causam maxime continet, quaeque apud omnes Orthodoxos non minus in confesso fuit, quam duae priores. Illa gratia Christi quae constat infusione fidei, charitatis, atque omnium donorum ad salutem infallibiliter efficiendam necessariorum, (hoc est, quae sanat animam, quae dat bonum velle et perficere) non datur hominibus ex antecedaneo intuitu ad meliores aliquas operationes aut dispositiones accipientium, neque negatur aliis ex antecedaneo intuitu ad pejores illorum operationes aut dispositiones non accipientium, sed ex mera Dei voluntate miserentis cujus vult, et cujus non vult non miserentis, absque omni respectu ad praevium discrimen personarum.

sections.title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 3: catholic doctrine — opposite always Pelagian/Semipelagian badge; they grant common offered mercy but make healing grace hang on prior merit
english: That this was catholic church doctrine is plain, first because the contrary was always the Pelagians’ and Semipelagians’ defense and as it were their badge. Though (as Arminians also now do) they granted a grace offered to all from mere mercy, yet the grace that heals, quickens, and justifies—and is not only offered by God but already possessed by man—they thought given only from antecedent merit of some good act or disposition God saw in the receiver and not in others.
sections.latin: Hanc fuisse doctrinam Catholicae Ecclesiae patet, 1. Quia contraria semper a Pelagianis et Semipelagianis defensa fuit, et ejus ea quasi proprium insigne habita. Nam utcunque (quod etiam Arminiani jam faciunt) gratiam quandam agnoverint ex mera Dei misericordia omnibus oblatam, tamen illam quae sanat, vivificat, et justificat, quaeque non offertur tantum ex parte Dei, sed jam possidetur ex parte hominis, illam, inquam, cenrebant datam nisi ex antecedente merito bonae alicujus operationis aut dispositionis quam in accipiente vidit Deus, in aliis non vidit.

sections.title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 3: Augustine on Pelagius — grace to the worthy; Prosper’s chronicle; Faustus — attracting mercy if given to the worthy
english: So Augustine on Pelagius himself (De gestis Palaestinis 14): he held God gives this grace to whoever is worthy to receive it. And Haeresis 88: the Pelagian error was that the grace by which we are freed from impiety is given according to our merits. Prosper’s Chronicle for 414: in that season Pelagius the Briton put forth his dogma against Christ’s grace, preaching that each is ruled to righteousness by his own will and receives as much grace as he deserves. For the Semipelagians hear their leader Faustus (lib. 1, c. 17): If the attracting God’s mercy is given to the worthy, you see it is already also spent on somehow serving by human effort. A little later: in the one you see attracting, he requires in every way a keeper of the precepts, so that by a little handle of will the called may be grasped.
sections.latin: Sic de Pelagio ipso scribit Augustinus, eum nempe tenuisse, donare Deum hanc gratiam ei qui fuerit dignus accipere, Cap. 14. De gestis Palaestinis. Et Haer. 88. idem Pater testatur Pelagianorum errorem fuisse, Quod gratia Dei qua liberamur ab impietate, secundum merita nostra detur. Sic etiam Prosper in Chron. ad annum 414. scribit, Hac tempestate Pelagius Brito dogma nominis sui contra gratiam Christi exserit, praedicans, unumquemque ad justitiam propria voluntate regi, tantamque accipere gratiam quantum meruerit. Jam pro Semipelagianis loquatur Faustus illorum antesignanus, Attrahentis Dei misericordia si dignis datur, advertis quia jam et studio humanae utcunque servitutis impenditur, Lib. 1. cap. 17. Paulo post, In quem perspicis attrahentem, requirit omnimodis praecepta servantem, ut per quandam voluntatis ansulam comprehendi valeat qui vocatur.

sections.title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 3: ‘merit’ here means any prior better operation/disposition for which grace is given to one not another — then Fathers deny such prerequisite (Aug. contra 2 Epist. Pelag.)
english: In all this mark: not even Pelagius denies grace is offered promiscuously to all, worthy and unworthy, from divine pity. He parts from the catholics in thinking it is always conferred from some special merit of those who receive it, and withheld from some special demerit of those denied it. In the Fathers here ‘merit’ means only any prior act or better disposition in one than another, with regard to which this Grace of Christ is given to one and not another. Second, our proposition’s truth is plain because the orthodox Fathers expressly deny that this saving grace prerequires a better act or condition in the receiver than in those not given it: whatever discrimination there is among men they profess as the effect of this grace received, not the motive cause of receiving it.
sections.latin: In hisce omnibus illud velim observetis, Ne ipsum quidem Pelagium negare gratiam offerri promiscue omnibus, dignis et indignis, ex miseratione Divina: sed in eo a Catholicis diversus abit, quod conferri eam semper et donari putet ex merito quodam speciali eorum quibus donatur, sicuti non dari ex demerito quodam speciali eorum quibus negatur. Meriti vero vocabulum apud Patres in hac controversia nil aliud sonat, quam antecedaneam operationem quamlibet aut dispositionem meliorem in uno quam alio, cujus intuitu datur haec gratia Christi uni et non alii. 2. Veritas praedictae nostrae propositionis inde liquet, quod Patres orthodoxi expresse negant, gratiam hanc salvantem praerequirere meliorem operationem aut conditionem ejus cui donatur, quam est eorum quibus non donatur: sed quicquid discriminis est inter homines, id effectum hujus gratiae acceptae, non causam motivam accipiendae, profitentur.
